compiled_state.description:
## The defect

The close precheck requires EVERY `- [ ]` acceptance criterion to be ticked before a ticket can
close. It has no way to record that a criterion is NOT APPLICABLE.

This breaks on any ticket whose ACs are branch-exclusive — the common "decide X, then: if A do
this / if B do that" shape, where satisfying one branch necessarily means the other is never
performed.

## Confirmed instance 2026-08-05

Bug `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1` asked for an operator decision (honor the inert
`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` field, or remove it) and carried both outcomes as ACs:

    - [ ] If HONORED: structural metric evaluation is gated on it, with a test proving ...
    - [ ] If REMOVED: the field, its coercion row and its config-surface entries go ...

The operator chose REMOVE. The implementing agent therefore could not satisfy the HONORED
branch — by construction, not by omission. The close gate refused the close until that box was
ticked, so the agent ticked a criterion describing work it had deliberately not done, and
posted a comment stating the tick means N/A rather than done. It did NOT use `--force-close`,
which was the right call.

Ticket authorship is a contributing cause and worth saying plainly: whoever writes a
decide-then-branch ticket creates this trap. But the gate offering no expression for N/A is
what converts an awkward ticket into a false record.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating

A ticked AC is load-bearing evidence in this system. The close gate reads it, the completion
verifier reasons over it, and reviewers treat it as an assertion that the work was done. Once
agents learn that ticking can mean "not applicable", the signal degrades for every ticket, not
just branch-exclusive ones — and the degradation is invisible, because a ticked box looks
identical either way.

The `[operator-attested]` tag already establishes the precedent that a criterion can be
satisfied by something other than in-repo work. This is the same shape: a criterion that is
legitimately not code-verifiable, for a different reason.

## Candidate approaches (weigh; not prescribed)

1. An explicit marker, e.g. `- [x] [n/a: <reason>]` or `- [~]`, that the precheck accepts and
   that records WHY. Mirrors `[operator-attested]`, so the vocabulary stays consistent.
2. Structured branch groups, so ACs can be declared mutually exclusive and the gate requires
   exactly one branch satisfied.
3. Author-side only: forbid branch-exclusive ACs and require the decision to be made before the
   ACs are written. Cheapest, but relies on discipline and does not help tickets already filed.

Option 3 alone is insufficient — the decide-then-branch shape is genuinely useful when a ticket
is filed before the operator has ruled, which is exactly how a573 and dce2 were written.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A criterion can be recorded as NOT APPLICABLE, with a reason, in a form the close gate
      accepts without a tick that falsely asserts completion.
- [ ] The completion verifier understands the marker too, so an N/A criterion is not later
      reported as unmet or as satisfied-without-evidence.
- [ ] A test proves a branch-exclusive ticket can close with one branch satisfied and the other
      marked N/A, and that a criterion marked N/A WITHOUT a reason is refused.
- [ ] The mechanism is documented where AC authors will see it, alongside `[operator-attested]`.
- [ ] `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1`'s falsely-ticked HONORED criterion is corrected to the new form, so
      the record stops asserting work that was deliberately not done.

## Provenance

Reported by the agent that hit it while closing a573. Recorded because the same shape is
already present on other open tickets that pair a decision with per-branch ACs.
compiled_state.title: The close gate cannot express an N/A acceptance criterion, so mutually-exclusive ACs force a false tick
